legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness", Haoran Ye, Yuxing Lu, Haonan Dong, Zhaochen Su, Guojie Song (Peking Univ., Google, HKUST). Preprint (no venue printed), dated September 22, 2026 on p1; arXiv:2609.24974v1 [cs.AI], 21 Sep 2026. Code: github.com/metaevo-ai/harness-zero. Note: models named (GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3, Qwen3.5-9B, DeepSeek-V4) are from the paper, not checked by me.

COVERAGE: 25 of 25 pages extracted; 101,791 chars. I read main text (p1-9) in full and appendix A start, D, E, F and G start. I only skimmed the references, plus appendix A (the rest of the evolution skill), B (harness-adaptation examples), C (reviewer prompt) and the rest of G (pattern descriptions). Figures not extracted.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Distilling an evolved harness into weights, with the harness removed at deployment, beats the same base model with the harness attached.
 number: macro-average 23.3% to 44.3%, versus 41.7% with the evolved harness h* attached.
 setup: Qwen3.5-9B base; LoRA SFT; three domains (SpreadsheetBench Verified 100 held-out tasks, AppWorld 168 test_normal tasks scored as scenario goal completion, USPTO Retrosynthesis 100 test tasks); target harness h is mini-SWE-agent with one Bash tool; single run pass@1. Per benchmark, base / with h* / distilled: SpreadsheetBench 31.0 / 39.0 / 44.0; AppWorld 26.8 / 48.2 / 58.9; USPTO 12.0 / 38.0 / 30.0.
 quote: "HARNESS-ZEROraises the macro average from 23.3% to 44.3%, a 21.0-point absolute gain and a 90.1% relative improvement. It also exceeds the 41.7% macro average of the base model equipped with h⋆."
 where: p7 (Table 2, Obs. 2)
2. Procedural behaviour distils well. Deep domain knowledge distils less well.
 number: USPTO 30.0% distilled vs 38.0% with h* (base 12.0%).
 setup: as above; USPTO h* adds reaction priors, candidate generation and SMILES validation tools.
 quote: "On USPTO, HARNESS-ZEROimproves over the base model (30.0% vs. 12.0%) but trails h⋆ (38.0%)."
 where: p7 (Obs. 3)
3. What makes the supervision work is harness-guided review of the student's own proposals. Stronger teacher trajectories or answer access do not help.
 number: USPTO test pass@1 under h: Harness-Zero 30.0; teacher rollout 12.0 (collection success 52.0); teacher under h* 3.0 (62.0); student under h* 12.0 (39.4); review with empty K 11.0 (44.2); review with oracle answer 15.0 (98.6). Base 12.0.
 setup: Qwen3.5-9B, same 500-task collection split, 2-epoch checkpoint, teacher/harnessing agent GPT-5.6 Sol.
 quote: "Directly fine-tuning on GPT-5.6 Sol trajectories leaves the student at the 12% base result, even though that source succeeds on 52.0% of the collection tasks."
 where: p7 (Table 3, Obs. 4-6)
 Trajectories collected under h* fail because of action-space mismatch: the distilled student "extensively attempts unavailable harness-tool calls" and exhausts the turn limit (p8).
4. The distilled model recovers behaviours that only appear under h*.
 number: 82.3% average recovery over 28 patterns (18 SpreadsheetBench, 6 USPTO, 4 AppWorld).
 setup: patterns kept only if at least 10 test tasks show them under h* but not under h, so the base model scores 0% by construction. Weak spots: AppWorld "Retrieve complete pages" 21/53 (40%) and "Read back mutations" 6/12 (50%).
 quote: "Averaged over the 28 patterns in Table 4, HARNESS-ZEROrecovers 82.3% of the harness-exclusive behaviors."
 where: p8 (Table 4, Obs. 7)
5. Inference-time, with no training, agent-as-harness (a reviewer agent that corrects each response) beats code-as-harness (evolved harness code wrapped around the model).
 number: 81.1% vs 78.1% (meta-harness) vs 68.6% (mini-SWE-agent). With empty K it is only 69.2%.
 setup: six benchmark-model settings (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GPT-5.6 Sol); the same model plays student and reviewer; h* is the one evolved on Qwen3.5-9B. Gains are mixed per setting. For example GPT-5.6 Sol on AppWorld is 96.4 (mini-SWE-agent), 94.6 (meta-harness) and 96.4 (agent-as-harness).
 quote: "Across the six settings in Table 1, agent-as-harness with the adapted K averages 81.1%, against 78.1% for meta-harness and 68.6% for mini-SWE-agent."
 where: p6 (Table 1)
6. General-purpose harnesses hurt the 9B base model.
 number: macro-average DeepAgents 20.5, Claude Code 15.9, versus 23.3 with mini-SWE-agent.
 setup: Qwen3.5-9B base, Table 2.
 quote: "Neither general-purpose harness benefits the base model."
 where: p7
7. Cost. Review adds latency and tokens during collection only, and nothing at deployment.
 number: 237.2 s per trial vs 100.1 s, about 2.4x, on USPTO.
 setup: agent-as-harness with evolved guidance vs mini-SWE-agent; at least two model calls per step.
 quote: "agent-as-harness with evolved guidance takes 237.2 s per trial on average, about2.4× the 100.1 s required by mini-SWE-agent."
 where: p24 (App. F). No token counts are given. No deployment-time latency of the distilled model is reported.

TRAINING SETUP (App. D/E, p22-23)
- Data: 487 SpreadsheetBench, 282 AppWorld and 500 USPTO trajectories.
- Filtering: SpreadsheetBench and AppWorld keep reward-1.0 trials only. USPTO keeps all trials, which gave higher test performance than successes only.
- Training: LoRA rank 32, alpha 32, batch 8, 65,536-token sequences, 2 epochs, peak learning rate 2e-4, seed 42. A separate model is trained per domain, with Tinker recipe SFT.
- The loss masks reviewer-perspective reasoning.
- h* evolved by Kimi K3 over 3 rounds with a skill-guided loop.

LIMITS (authors)
- Needs a capable harnessing model. On weaker students review turns harmful: USPTO agent-as-harness minus meta-harness is +1.0 (GPT-5.6 Sol), +4.0 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), -1.0 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) and -12.0 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). The weakest model had 66.0% of steps replaced (p23-24).
- SFT may not fully internalise deep domain knowledge.
- Some harness mechanisms, such as context management, are not expressible as student responses.
- The authors say it "does not remove the need for a harness, but narrows what that harness must provide."
- Review of every proposal is costly. Selective review and preference learning (the rejected/preferred pairs go unused) are left to future work.
- My observations. Single seed (42) and single run pass@1. Test sets are small (100 tasks for two benchmarks), with no confidence intervals. Only one student size (9B). The distilled model is not compared to RL or to a prompted-with-harness frontier student at this scale beyond h*. There is no SFT-vs-RL comparison, and "RL" appears only as related work. The distilled model sits under the same mini-SWE-agent h it was trained for, so transfer to other harnesses is not shown. The ablation (Table 3) is USPTO only.

BUILDS ON: Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026); DeepAgents (LangChain, 2025); mini-SWE-agent (SWE-agent Team, 2025); EvoHarness-RL (Ning et al., 2026a); OPHSD (Zhao et al., 2026); Tinker recipe (Thinking Machines Lab, 2025); harness-weight co-evolution work (Chen et al. 2026a-c, Kim et al. 2026 WHALE, Hebbar et al. 2026); Le et al. 2026 (a multi-harness RL study showing harness changes matter more than training method).

CODE: none worth keeping. The prompt snippets are in App. C and E. The student system prompt "Prompt 2" is on p22-23 (one `execute` bash tool).

FIGURES: Figure 1 (p4) is the pipeline overview: evolve and adapt h* into private K, harnessing agent PASS/REPLACE at the response boundary, SFT, deploy under h alone. This is the quickest way to see the method. I did not extract the figure.

PROBLEMS: None. No embedded instructions found. Text extraction is clean, but Figure 1 text is jumbled.

KEY VERBATIM QUOTES FOR THE NOTE
- p1: "With the specialized harness removed at deployment, HARNESS-ZEROimproves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached."
- p7: "Effective supervision comes from harness-guided review, not from stronger demonstrations alone."
- p9: "HARNESS-ZEROtherefore does not remove the need for a harness, but narrows what that harness must provide"
